title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — Rom 5 conclude: propagated sin; each own; die by natural communion, not in Adam's person
pass_a_gloss: Tip conclusion on Rom 5: when Paul says sin entered through one man, Placeus hears sin born from Adam and spread into all—not the singular paradise act imputed. The slogan 'all sinned in Adam' (which Paul does not say) means each by his own inborn proper sin from that origin. Dying in Adam is by natural communion with him, not by being in Adam's person; living in Christ is by supernatural communion—not by being in Christ's person. More when the Theses come. Natural tip before GAR Resp. 1.
pass_b_english: Let us conclude, then: when the same Apostle says that through one man sin entered the world, it is to be understood not as that singular actual sin which that one man committed, but as the sin born from him and spread and propagated into all men. And when it is said that all sinned in Adam (though he does not say that), it is to be understood that all sinned—not by that one singular actual sin of Adam imputed to them, but each by his own inborn and proper sin, which takes its origin from that of Adam. We die, then, in Adam—that is, by the force of the natural communion that joins us to Adam, not in Adam's own person; and we are made alive in Christ, not in the very person of Jesus Christ, but by the force of our supernatural communion with him: but of this again when we come to the Theses.
source_text: Concludamus igitur, cum idem Apostolus ait, per unum hominem peccatum in mundum introisse, intelligendum esse non singulare illud actuale peccatum quod unus ille homo commisit, sed peccatum ab illo natum, & in omnes homines sparsum ac propagatum: Et, cum ait, omnes peccasse in Adamo (quanquam id non dicit) intelligendum esse omnes peccasse, non uno illo singulari peccato actuali Adami illis imputato, sed suo quemque, sibi infito ac proprio peccato, quod ab illo Adami ducit originem. Morimur ergo in Adamo; id est, vi communionis naturalis quae nobis cum Adamo intercedit, non autem in ipsa Adami persona; & vivificamur in Christo, non in ipsa persona Iesu Christi, sed vi communionis nostrae supernaturalis cum ea: sed hac de re rursus cum ad Theses ventum fuerit.
